Based on the foregoing provisions, upon compliance with the requirements on income, population, and land area, the interested component city, through a resolution of its sanggunian, must submit an application for conversion into a highly urbanized city before the Office of the President, attaching thereto documentary proof showing compliance with the requisites. In the event thet the President declares the component city as highly urbanized, such declaration will then be the subject of a plebiscite in the city proposed to be converted, to determine whether or not the registered voters thereof are in conformity with the conversion. A positive outcome in the plebiscite is a ratification by the people of the city's conversion, and is considered as the final step in the component citys conversion into a highly urbanized one. As regards your second query, paragraph 4 of Section 5, ARTICLE VI of the 1987 Constitution is unambiguous in providing that the Congress shall make a reapportionment of legislative districts based on the standards provided in the same section. Thus, the entitlement of a city to a separate congressional seat, as well as its number of legislative seats to which it is entitled, must be provided for through a law duly enacted by Congress. Consequently, your desire to have an additional legislative seat in your city may be properly addressed by lobbying for the passage of a law providing for such legislative seat. We hope we have enlightened you on the matters pertaining to your request. Very truly yours, Director III LS: 03
